ledger.note: 1 September 1961: the Eritrean armed struggle begins at the Battle of Adal. "The war started on 1 September 1961 with the Battle of Adal"; Hamid Idris Awate and his companions engaged the Ethiopian army and police. The fighters (the ELF, then the EPLF from August 1973) held no ground yet.

region.text: the western lowlands, where the Battle of Adal began the war

ledger.note: 1975-1977: the fronts liberate nearly all of Eritrea. "All of Eritrea was liberated with the exception of Asmara, Massawa, Assab and Barentu"; the EPLF page says "From 1975 to 1977, the ELF and EPLF outnumbered the Ethiopian army". The page gives the span, not the year: 1977 closes it.

ledger.note: May 1991: the rebels win and hold Eritrea de facto; "In April 1993, the Eritrean people voted almost unanimously in favour of independence" and the United Nations admitted Eritrea on 28 May 1993; the Third Congress in 1994 turned the front into a political movement.

wars.name: Eritrean War of Independence
wars.outcome: EPLF victory: Afabet 1988, Massawa 1990, Asmara on 24 May 1991; independence confirmed by the April 1993 referendum.
wars.note: The ethiopia dossier (af-01-c) records the contest with the counterpart string 'Eritrean independence fighters', which is this slug.

wars.name: ELF-EPLF civil wars
wars.outcome: The ELF declared war on the EPLF in mid-1972 and the first civil war ended without a clear winner in 1974; the fronts reconciled in 1975; clashes resumed (August 1980) and most ELF fighters retreated into Sudan by 1981.
wars.note: The EPLF merged with the ELF's Central Leadership in 1987 (Second Congress).

sources.title: Eritrean War of Independence
sources.note: 1 September 1961 Battle of Adal; 1975-1977 all but four towns liberated; May-July 1978 Derg counter-offensive; Afabet 1988; Massawa February 1990; Asmara 24 May 1991; referendum April 1993.

sources.title: Eritrean People's Liberation Front
sources.note: EPLF formed August 1973 from the ELF; headquarters Nakfa 1976-1991; 1978 strategic withdrawal; Afabet March 1988; Massawa 1990; Derg overthrown May 1991; Third Congress 1994.

notes: New dossier of type rebel, requested by af-01-c (it asked for 'eritrean-people-s-liberation-front, 1961-1991'). Pages opened: Eritrean War of Independence, Eritrean People's Liberation Front (2). The ELF (1961) and EPLF (August 1973) are drawn as one rebel colour; the page treats them as two fronts that fought each other in 1972-74 and 1980-81 and merged in 1987; a gap-filler could split an 'Eritrean Liberation Front' dossier (1961-1981). The ethiopia dossier (af-01-c) records contest_start 1961/9 and contest_end 1991 with the counterpart string 'Eritrean independence fighters' over all of Eritrea; its 1991 loss goes to state-of-eritrea. The holdings between 1978 and 1988 (the Sahel pocket round Nakfa) and the land taken at Afabet are not on the pages: those regions are radii at confidence-2 events. Gazetteer note: Natural Earth's Eritrean admin-1 names are scrambled in the gazetteer (e.g. 'Semenawi Keyih Bahri' resolves to the Anseba region and 'Debub' to the Northern Red Sea region); this dossier uses country, Gash Barka, places and coordinates only. Gazetteer names needed: Nakfa, Afabet, Barentu (all given as coordinates).
